title: spec review: Q5 v4: orchestrator/planner_scorecard.py + `scorecard --planner-routing` — Planner outcomes by model × decision type × band × class × architectural, non-inferiority evidence per class, economics (P7, P13, P16)
spec:
Why: no code joins Planner invocations to downstream engineering outcomes; premium_summary (planner_runs.py:843) counts launches and tokens only. The router (planner_router.py, merged) needs class_evidence and the brief (P7/P13/P16) a Planner scorecard with cold-start priors and a CLI. Spec reviews T-0683 and of T-0710 are folded in: producer named and a dependency (planner_telemetry.py, merged as T-0708), explicit min_samples source, literal criteria mapping with correct comparator signs, guarded telemetry import, terminal-state restriction for first-pass metrics. READ-SIDE: the scorecard stays empty in production until Wave B wires planner_runs to emit invocation rows (stated so reviewers do not expect a populated card after this merge).
What: new module orchestrator/planner_scorecard.py plus cli.py flag `scorecard --planner-routing [--json]`.
- Inputs: invocation rows via planner_telemetry.read_invocations_with_malformed(root) (rows merged by launch_id with fields launch_id, goal_id, kind, payload_keys, decision_type, model, tier, band, task_class, architectural, started_at, material, reescalation, total_tokens, usd, latency_s, outcome), bus tasks from root/tasks/*.json, spec_review and review tasks among them. Wrap `from . import planner_telemetry` in try/except ImportError so a missing module degrades to an empty card with card["error"] = "planner_telemetry unavailable". Malformed lines counted in card["malformed"].
- min_samples: explicit parameter wins; else cfg planner.routing.min_samples when int (the [planner.routing] table lands with this goal's pool.toml task and may be absent); else cfg promotion.min_samples; else 20.
- Attribution window: an invocation owns the goal's execute tasks whose lineage root (attribution.lineage(task)["root"]) has created_at >= invocation started_at and < the next invocation's started_at for the same goal (or +inf); fix rounds belong to their root's owner. A kind held invocation additionally owns the fix-round task whose constraints.fix_round_for equals that invocation's held task id (payload_keys[0] split at ':').
- Terminal roots: a root is terminal when merged_into is set, or status == "failed", or pipeline.first_green_at is present. first_pass_rate, fix_round_rate and avg_fix_rounds use terminal roots only in numerator and denominator (in-flight roots are excluded, never counted as successes); downstream_accepted_rate counts all owned roots (unresolved = not accepted).
- group_key(row) -> f"{model}|{decision_type}|{band}|{task_class}|{'arch' if architectural else 'plain'}".
- build(root=STATE, *, cfg=None, min_samples=None) -> {"groups": {key: metrics}, "n", "malformed", "min_samples", "read_side_only": True}; metrics per group: n, material_rate, downstream_accepted_rate, first_pass_rate (terminal roots with pipeline.lineage_fix_rounds in (0, None) and no fix-round children), fix_round_rate, avg_fix_rounds, gate_red_rate (pipeline.gate_reds > 0), review_request_changes_rate (review tasks whose inputs[0] is an owned id, verdict from review_verdict or result.verdict == request_changes), spec_review_approval_rate (same for spec_review role, verdict approve), replanning_rate (a later invocation of the same goal with decision_type architectural_replan), reescalation_rate (rows reescalation True), human_intervention_rate (None unless planner_telemetry.interactive_by_goal returns a row for the goal with a day after started_at; the call wrapped in try/except Exception -> None), tokens_mean, usd_mean, latency_mean, terminal_roots (count), evidence "sufficient"|"insufficient" (n >= min_samples).
- Thresholds. CRITERIA_MAP = {"first_pass_rate": ("first_pass_delta", ">=", -0.02), "avg_fix_rounds": ("fix_rounds_delta", "<=", 0.05), "gate_success": ("gate_success_delta", ">=", -0.02)} read from promotion.CRITERIA by those keys (overridable via cfg["promotion"]); their signs agree with promotion.py. review_request_changes_rate uses this module's own constant REVIEW_CHANGES_MAX_DELTA = 0.10 with comparator "<=" (promotion's review_findings_delta is a negative findings-count criterion with the opposite meaning and is NOT used). REESCALATION_MAX = 0.2. gate_success = 1 - gate_red_rate. An equal candidate/baseline pair (all deltas 0) must pass every comparison.
- class_evidence(model, decision_type, band, task_class, architectural, *, root=STATE, cfg=None, min_samples=None) -> {"n", "noninferior": True|False|None, "deltas": {metric: candidate - baseline}, "failed": [metric names], "reescalation_rate", "baseline_model"}: baseline group = same class with model == cfg [models].planner (fallback: rows with tier fable). None when either group has n < min_samples; False when any comparison fails or reescalation_rate > REESCALATION_MAX (failed lists "reescalation"); True otherwise. Tokens, usd, latency never enter the verdict (docstring + test).
- economics(root=STATE) -> per model {"planner_usd_per_accepted_goal", "planner_tokens_per_accepted_goal", "pipeline_usd_after_planning" (mean over invocations of the sum of scorecard.by_task usd for owned tasks), "expected_total_cost_after_planning": {decision_type: mean(planner usd + pipeline usd)}}; accepted goals via scorecard.accepted_goals(root).
- format(card) -> text table sorted by key with a first line 'read-side only: rows appear once planner_runs emits invocations' when n == 0; format_evidence(evidence) one line. cli.py: `sc.add_argument("--planner-routing", action="store_true")`, dispatch to build/format (json with --json), ap.error when combined with --planner or --parallelism (same style as the existing pair).
acceptance: tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_groups_by_model_type_band_class_arch — rows written with planner_telemetry.record_launch/record_usage/record_materiality under a sandbox root for two models and two decision types produce four group keys with n, material_rate and downstream_accepted_rate from owned tasks in the attribution window

tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_attribution_window_terminal_roots_and_fix_rounds — a root task created after invocation A and its fix round created after invocation B both count toward A; a held-kind invocation owns the fix round with constraints.fix_round_for; an in-flight root (no merged_into, not failed, no first_green_at) is excluded from first_pass_rate and fix_round_rate but counted as not accepted

tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_class_evidence_noninferior_equivalent_worse_and_insufficient — opus identical to fable (all deltas 0, including review_request_changes_rate) gives noninferior True with failed empty; opus with first_pass_rate 0.3 lower gives False with failed naming first_pass_rate; opus with review_request_changes_rate 0.3 higher gives False naming review_request_changes_rate; n below min_samples gives None; a group with 1e9 tokens and 0 usd changes no verdict
tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_reescalation_penalises_class — reescalation_rate 0.5 on an otherwise equal class gives noninferior False with failed containing reescalation

tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_cli_flag_min_samples_source_and_malformed_tolerance — `scorecard --planner-routing --json` under a sandbox root prints a card with read_side_only True, groups and malformed 1 for a runs dir containing one malformed line; min_samples comes from [planner.routing] when present, else [promotion], else 20; a patched ImportError for planner_telemetry yields card error text instead of a crash

risks.issue: Attribution window double-owns fix-round tasks: the general rule assigns every execute task (root or fix round) to the invocation owning its lineage root's window ('fix rounds belong to their root's owner'), but the spec then says a kind=held invocation 'additionally owns' the same fix-round task via constraints.fix_round_for. That is two invocations owning one task. Concretely: invocation A owns root T1 (created_at in A's window); later invocation B (kind=held, started_at after A) triggers fix round T2 with constraints.fix_round_for=T1. By the general rule T2 is owned by A (T2's lineage root T1 falls in A's window); by the held clause T2 is ALSO owned by B. economics() sums scorecard.by_task usd 'for owned tasks' per invocation, so T2's usd is counted in both A's and B's pipeline_usd_after_planning, inflating both and any downstream total that sums across invocations/models. The same double-owned id also inflates review_request_changes_rate/spec_review_approval_rate denominators for both A and B if a review targets T2 (those use 'review tasks whose inputs[0] is an owned id').

The 'held task id (payload_keys[0] split at \':\')' parsing rule assumes a colon-delimited payload_keys[0] format that no existing producer emits — the only real record_launch call site (tests/test_planner_telemetry.py) uses kind="task", payload_keys=["T-0002"] with no colon, and there is no merged producer for kind="held" invocations at all (record_launch has zero non-test callers today). The split is harmless when no colon is present (returns the whole string) but the format is invented rather than sourced from an actual producer, so it should be stated as an assumption to confirm against Wave B's held-invocation producer rather than asserted as fact.

suggested_spec_changes: Make fix-round ownership exclusive: either (a) drop the 'kind held invocation additionally owns the fix-round task' clause and let the held invocation's contribution to economics/review-rate come only through its own directly-launched tasks in its window, or (b) if a held invocation should own the specific fix-round task it triggered, explicitly exclude that task from the root owner's owned-task set so no task id appears in two invocations' owned sets — state which one wins.

Confirm the payload_keys[0] format for kind="held" invocations against the actual Wave B producer (not yet merged) before committing to 'split at colon'; if the producer will emit a bare task id (matching today's only real example), drop the split-at-colon instruction and just use payload_keys[0] directly.
